title: SPA/641/2019 of SELAQUI ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION CAMPUS CHAKRATA ROAD Vs LOKPAL UTTARAKHAND TECHNCIAL UNIVERSITY SUDDHOWALA DEHRADUN

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 641 of 2019
Selaqui Academy of Higher Education
Campus Chakrata Road and another
 ...........appellants
Vs.
Lokpal Uttarakhand Technical University Suddhowala Deharadun
and others ...........Respondents

With
Special Appeal No. 645 of 2019
Selaqui Academy of Higher Education
Campus and another .........................appellants
Vs.
Hon'ble Lokpal Uttarakhand Technical University Suddhowala
Dehradun and others ..................................Respondents
Presents:
Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned Advocate for the petitioners.
Ms. Gurbani Singh, learned Advocate holding brief of Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, learned
Advocate for respondent No.1.
Mr. B.S. Parihar, learned Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent
No.12.
Dated: 2nd July, 2019
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral)
 This appeal is preferred against the interlocutory
order passed by the learned Single Judge on 14.06.2019, and
a modification is sought of the order dated 08.05.2019 passed
earlier in the writ petition.
2. The appellants herein filed the present writ petition
questioning the order passed by the Lokpal on 03.03.2014
and 25.04.2014, whereby they were directed not to recover
additional fees from certain students pursuing B.Tech.

2
courses in their institution. As a result, the unofficial
respondents in both the writ petitions completed their B.Tech.
course on payment of the reduced fee, and have since left for
their respective places of residence in the States of Jammu
and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Uttarakhand, Assam, Uttar
Pradesh, New Delhi, etc.
3. As notices in the writ petition could not be served
on the unofficial respondents, and as these students were
located all over the country, the learned Single Judge, by his
order dated 08.05.2019, directed the appellants-writ
petitioners to take steps by substitutive mode of service by
issuing publication in a National Daily News paper, having
circulation throughout the country, for affecting service on
the unofficial respondents. The publication of notice was to
be done in one national daily newspaper which was of wide
circulation.
4. Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned Counsel for the
appellants-writ petitioners, would submit that the cost of
publication, in a national newspaper such as the Times of
India, is Rs.4.5 lacs per publication; and, since there are two
appeals, the expenditure to be incurred for such publication
would exceed Rs.9.0 Lacs. Learned counsel would submit
that this Court may consider permitting the appellants-writ
petitioners to cause publication in the local newspapers at the
respective places, or to direct the Registry, on deposit of the
prescribed publication charges by the appellants-writ
petitioners, to take steps to cause publication.
5. We see no reason to accede to either of the requests.
No rule, which requires the High Court Registry, to cause
paper publication, for effecting service of notices on the
unofficial respondents, has been brought to our notice. It is
for the appellants-writ petitioners, who have approached this

3
Court and have sought relief, to take necessary steps to cause
service of notices, in the writ petitions, on the unofficial
respondents. For grant of permission to the appellants-writ
petitioners, to cause publication in the local newspapers of
the respective States, this Court would be required to first
ascertain whether or not the local newspapers, in which the
appellants-writ petitioners seek to cause publication, have
wide circulation in the area. Since the unofficial respondents
are spread over several States, this exercise would be required
to be undertaken for each of the States. We see no reason,
therefore, to interfere with the order of the learned Single
Judge in directing publication in a national newspaper having
circulation all over the country.
6. Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel for the
appellants-writ petitioners, would then submit that since the
unofficial respondents have completed their B.Tech course, on
payment of lesser tuition fee in view of the order of the
Lokpal, it would be extremely difficult for the appellants to
now recover the differential fees from them by filing Suits at
different States; and, even if they were to succeed later in the
writ petition, they may not be in any position to recover the
differential amount due from them. Learned counsel would
submit that this Court may consider recording the
submission of the appellants-writ petitioners that they would
not seek recovery of the differential amount due from the
unofficial respondents in these two appeals; and, instead,
permit the appellants-writ petitioners to confine their
challenge in the writ petition only to the order of the Lok Pal
so that, in case they were to succeed in the writ petition later,
they would be in a position to recover the actual tuition fees
from students, studying in their institution, in future.

4
7. In the light of the submission now made before us,
by Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel for the appellants-writ
petitioners, that they do not intend to recover the differential
amount from the unofficial respondents in these two appeals,
and they intend confining their prayer in the writ petition only
to the validity of the orders passed by the Lokpal, suffice it to
permit the appellants-writ petitioners to file a modification
application before the learned Single Judge seeking deletion of
the unofficial respondents from the array of respondents in
the writ petitions, and for recall of the order dated
08.05.2019. Since no relief would now be sought against the
unofficial respondents, we have no reason to doubt that the
learned Single Judge, before whom the matter is listed
tomorrow, will consider granting the appellants-writ
petitioners reasonable time to move a modification application
for modification/recall of the order dated 08.05.2019 in terms
of the undertaking, furnished on their behalf, by their
counsel.
8. The special appeals are disposed of accordingly. No
costs.
9. Let a certified copy of this order be issued to the
learned counsel for the parties, today itself, on payment of the
prescribed charges.

(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, CJ.)
 02.07.2019
Sanjay
